markdown: ## TL;DR I audited the web UI for icon-only controls without accessible names, native `title` use, and inconsistent wording. The real defect was narrower than the task suggested: the global tooltip helper strips a control's `title` on first hover or focus, so an icon-only control named only by `title` loses its accessible name after the first interaction. I gave the four affected components their own `aria-label`, unified one tooltip phrase, added a template-wide guard test, and wrote the audit at `docs/qa/2026-11-labels-tooltips-audit-qa.md`. Two review rounds found false negatives in the guard; round 3 replaces the ad hoc regexes with one quote-aware tag pattern. The scoped `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed. ## Work and rationale I started with a grep for `title="` and `:title=` across `src/ui-app/src`, which returned about 100 hits. Most are not native bubbles: `src/ui-app/src/lib/tooltip.ts` installs one body-level tooltip that restyles any `title` into a popup. Replacing all of them would be a large refactor, so I left them and recorded that in the audit. The more useful question was whether each icon-only control has a name. A throwaway Bun scanner in `/tmp` (not committed) found no unnamed controls at all. I checked it against a synthetic icon button first, because a zero from a regex can just mean the regex is wrong. A second scan, for icon-only controls whose only name was a `title`, found eight. The tooltip code explains why that matters: `enter()` calls `textFor()`, which removes `title` and stores it in `data-tip`, so the name survives only until the first `mouseover` or `focusin`. Three of the eight were `FloatingHeads` head buttons whose `` already names them. The other five were real: - `IntegrationStatusBar.vue`: the pipeline collapse toggle. - `AgentCard.vue`: the instructions expand/collapse toggle. - `AgentModelModal.vue`: two favorite star buttons, one per state. - `DiffView.vue`: the previous-file and next-file arrows. I added `aria-label` to each and kept `title`, so the styled tooltip still shows. I considered a central fix in `tooltip.ts` that copies `title` into `aria-label` for controls without visible text, and rejected it for this pass because it renames any control that goes through the helper. It is a listed follow-up. For wording, the drawer's full-screen diff button said "Open the full-screen diff view" while the other diff controls say "Open full-screen diff". I unified the drawer to the shorter form and checked that no test asserted the old string. The removal and dismissal verbs ("Remove attachment", "Delete schedule", "Dismiss this error", "Dismiss notification") differ, but choosing one verb is a product decision, so I documented them. The regression test is `src/ui-app/tests/icon-control-names.test.ts`. Its main assertion is a template-wide ratchet that fails if any button or link under `src/ui-app/src` has no visible text and no name attribute (or a non-empty ``). It also pins the four new `aria-label` values and the shared diff wording. I wrote it as a source scan rather than a mounted-component test, because mounting `AgentModelModal` and `DiffView` needs store and route setup that would dwarf the check. ## Review rounds Round 1 found two false negatives. The open-tag regex stopped at the first `>`, so `:disabled="i > 0"` (present in `LoginView.vue`) could make an unnamed control look like it had text. A blanket `v-bind=` exemption also skipped any bound control. I made the open-tag match quote-aware and removed the exemption. The template-wide scan still finds nothing once the exemption is gone, so no real control was hiding behind it. I also added a macOS Hub paragraph to the audit, checked by reading `macos/RepoOSHub/HubSidebarControls.swift`: its icon-only controls pair `.help()` with `.accessibilityLabel()`, which is the right tool in a native app. Round 2 found the same class in a second place. The body cleanup still stripped child tags with a quote-blind `<[^>]+>`, so a child such as `` left residue that counted as visible text, and the title-only control above it passed unnoticed. I reproduced it before changing anything. The fix in round 3 defines one quote-aware tag fragment (`TAG_BODY`) and uses it for the open tag, child tags and `` alike. The `` check also reads `alt` only from its own quoted attribute. Fixtures cover a `>` in a child `v-if`, a child `:class` ternary and a child ``. All 18 cases in the file pass. ## Approaches tried I first considered replacing every `title` with a per-component tooltip, and rejected it as out of scope since the styled tooltip already works and the real defect is the lost name. I also considered a headless Playwright pass to read computed accessible names after hover. The task allows headless checks only for visual verification, and a static guard plus the tooltip-code reasoning covered the same class more cheaply. I did not run a visual check. ## Challenges and blockers The first guard attempt used `fileURLToPath(new URL(..., import.meta.url))`, which fails under the UI vitest config because `import.meta.url` is not a `file:` URL. Using `__dirname`, as the sibling `mobile-touch-affordances.test.ts` does, fixed it. Running `bunx vitest run` without the UI config failed in unrelated suites with `localStorage` undefined. Using `--config src/ui-app/vite.config.ts` fixed that, and the six affected suites passed (94 tests). In round 2 the scoped gate's remote validation failed with "gate exit 137" during `bun install`, before any test ran. A rerun passed in 450s. I did not establish the cause of the first failure, only that it did not recur. The scoped check's `tests` step is skipped locally because the remote runner executes the suite (`REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS=1`). The full-suite verdict is left to RepoOS. No visual or screen-reader check was run. The change adds attributes and one wording change, so no layout or styling was expected to move. The audit states that a human screen-reader check of the four fixed controls has not been done. ## Key learnings A title-only name is a latent accessibility bug whenever a helper rewrites `title` at runtime. The tooltip helper did its job for sighted users and quietly removed the only name for everyone else. Controls that rely on `title` for their name should also carry `aria-label`, and the guard now enforces that for icon-only controls. Template scans that match tags with regexes are fragile in one specific way: a `>` inside any quoted attribute, on any tag, can end a match early. Fixing the open tag and leaving the child-tag cleanup alone is an incomplete fix. Using one quote-aware fragment everywhere removes the class rather than the instance. The guard still does not evaluate computed names, so a control built from a child component with its own name can slip past. The audit says so. ## Generated change summary Base tree: `07738e1f6eebdc4e555b071005edec6d90ce4258` Source tree: `89fdf25735b52885cb5053f977bfd8ffa9280775` - M src/ui-app/tests/icon-control-names.test.ts: +25 / −6
